original_question: Does every subspace of ℓ1(Γ), for an uncountable index set Γ, admit a norming Markushevich basis?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6.5: the paper isolates the question “Does every subspace of ℓ1(Γ), with Γ uncountable, admit a norming M-basis?” as a special case of the general heredity problem for norming Markushevich bases. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s exact special-case target: it asks about subspaces of ℓ1(Γ), keeps the requirement that Γ be uncountable, and asks for existence of a norming Markushevich basis. This is essentially Problem 6.5 in the paper, introduced immediately after the general heredity problem in Problem 6.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
missing_details: To make it fully stand-alone, quantify explicitly: “for every uncountable set Γ and every closed linear subspace Y of ℓ1(Γ) …”.

Unpack “norming Markushevich basis”: a biorthogonal system {(yα,yα*)}_{α∈A} in Y×Y* that is fundamental (span{yα} is dense in Y) and total (equivalently, span{yα*} is weak*-dense in Y*). Section 2 supplies this terminology. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

State the norming condition quantitatively, as in Definition 2.1: there exists λ ≥ 1 such that ||y|| ≤ λ sup{|f(y)| : f ∈ span{yα*}, ||f|| ≤ 1} for all y ∈ Y. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

Do not broaden the question to countably norming M-bases or Plichko spaces; the paper treats that as a separate nearby problem (Problem 6.6), not as Problem 6.5. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

Do not insert extra hypotheses such as WLD, complemented, Asplund, or separable; the official problem is exactly the unrestricted subspace question for ℓ1(Γ). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
The scalar field is left implicit in the paper’s Banach-space setting, so a faithful rewrite should not introduce an extra real-only or complex-only restriction.
refined_question: For every uncountable set Γ and every closed linear subspace Y of ℓ1(Γ), does Y admit a norming Markushevich basis; that is, does there exist a biorthogonal system {(yα,yα*)}_{α∈A} ⊂ Y×Y* such that span{yα : α∈A} is dense in Y, span{yα* : α∈A} is weak*-dense in Y*, and for some λ ≥ 1 one has ||y|| ≤ λ sup{|f(y)| : f ∈ span{yα* : α∈A}, ||f|| ≤ 1} for every y ∈ Y?
justification: Section 6 first states the general heredity problem for norming M-bases (Problem 6.1), then proves a positive case for WLD subspaces (Theorem 6.3), and immediately afterward says that the simplest candidate for a counterexample is ℓ1(Γ), isolating exactly Problem 6.5. Definition 2.1 provides the precise meaning of “norming M-basis,” while the preceding Section 2 terminology gives the fundamental/total content of an M-basis. Example 2.3 also explains why spaces with long unconditional bases are natural ambient examples in this discussion. So the faithful sharpening is not a broader heredity question and not the separate Plichko/countably norming variant, but precisely the ℓ1(Γ)-subspace question stated above. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
